long_biography.plain_text:
Henri Krijnen turned Krijco into a major Dutch operator of gaming machines and amusement centres. His brother Joe joined the flourishing business in 1971, helping make it a family company. At its height, Krijco ran fourteen centres and placed a substantial machine estate in hospitality venues. The brothers eventually delegated daily management while remaining owners and active industry participants.

Krijnen's fascination with mechanical entertainment extended beyond business. Across five decades he assembled fairground, dance and theatre organs, orchestrions, jukeboxes, automata and early gaming machines, installing many in a private collection in the Netherlands. He also co-wrote a history of jukeboxes and gaming machines and organised a related exhibition at Amersfoort's Museum Flehite.
